chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Khalid and Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, all together, from Al-Qasim ibn Urwah, from Abdul-Hamid Al-Taiy, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding the testimony of the owned slave, he said: 'When he is just (adl), his testimony is valid. The first one to reject the testimony of the owned slave was Umar ibn Al-Khattab, and that is when a slave came to him regarding a testimony, so he said, 'If I establish the testimony, I fear for my self, and if I conceal it, I would sin with my Lord.' So he said, 'Give your testimony. Indeed, we will not validate the testimony of a slave after you.'
ai.seo_question: What is the condition for an owned slave's testimony to be valid in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies that the testimony of an owned slave (mamluk) is legally valid provided he is 'adl' (just/upright), challenging the general Sunni practice of excluding slaves from testimony. It cites Umar ibn al-Khattab as the first to reject such testimony due to the specific fear of retaliation by the master, but clarifies that this was a contextual restriction for that individual rather than a permanent legal prohibition. This highlights the Shia emphasis on the moral integrity ('adalah') of the witness over their social status.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Khalid and Al Husayn Bin Saeed, both together, from Al Qasim Bin Urwat, from Abdul Hameed Al Taiy, from Muhammad Bin Muslim,

(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> regarding the testimony of the owned slave, having said: ‘When it was just, so the testimony is allowed. The first one to reject a testimony of the owned slave was Umar Bin Al-Khattab, and that is (when) a slave was brought to him regarding a testimony, so he (the slave) said, ‘If the testimony is established, I fear for myself, and if I were to conceal it, I would have a sinful heart with my Lord<sup>azwj</sup>’. So he (Umar) said, ‘Give your testimony. But, after you we will not allow any slave to testify’.
en.sarwar: 2. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Khalid and al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id all from al- Qasim ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Urwah from ‘Abd al-Hamid al-Ta’iy from Muhammad ibn Muslim who has narrated the following:

“About the testimony of a slave abu ‘Abd Allah, Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘If he is a just man it is permissible. The first one who rejected the testimony of a slave was ‘Umar ibn al-Khattab. Once a slave was brought before him to testify and he said, ‘If I testify I fear for myself; if I hide, it is a sin for me before my Lord.’ He (‘Umar) then said, ‘Testify, but after you I will not allow any slave to testify.’”
